definition: Kilo Code is an open-source artificial intelligence coding agent for software development.
details: It can generate and modify source code, execute commands, debug software, and perform development tasks from natural language instructions. Kilo Code is model-agnostic and can work with hundreds of large language models rather than being tied to a single AI provider. The software is available as an extension for Visual Studio Code and JetBrains integrated development environments, through a command-line interface, and through cloud-based agents. Kilo Code was acquired by Anaconda in July 2026.

explainer.lead: An open-source AI coding agent that generates and modifies code, runs commands and debugs from natural-language instructions. It is model-agnostic, so teams are not locked to one provider.

tiers.eli5: Like a coding assistant that works with whichever brain you plug in, rather than one company's brain only.
tiers.practitioner: Used inside VS Code and JetBrains, via a command line, or as cloud agents; the pitfall is granting command execution too freely, so sandboxing and review matter.
tiers.paperLevel: An agentic software-development tool accepting natural-language instructions to edit source, execute commands and debug; it supports many large language models rather than a single one, and was acquired by Anaconda in July 2026.

explainer.example: A developer types a request in the editor; the agent edits the files, runs the test command and reports the failing test.
